html:
SMTO-LLM-0038 — SMTO couldn't get a reply from the model

GUID: 5274ff6b-f72c-43bf-9150-16ab6f782a66
Slug: model-error
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • SMTO asked the model for its next step, but the request failed and SMTO couldn't tell why. The Run may have stopped; steps it finished earlier are not undone.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, expand Main, and select Check saved model. This tests the saved model connection directly and often reveals the real cause, such as an unreachable server.
  2. If the check fails, make sure the computer or service running the model is switched on and reachable, and that the Endpoint and API key shown there are still correct. A stopped model server or an expired key are common reasons a model request fails.
  3. If the Run stopped, read its activity in the conversation to see which steps already finished, then ask the Agent to continue only the rest. Steps the Run finished before the failed request stay done, so repeating them could do the same work twice.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passing checks, and the Agent replies to your follow-up.

If it still fails

  • If the model server looks healthy but this keeps happening, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete saved data or turn off security checks to get past it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model client call failed with an exception that carried no specific error_kind, so TracingLLMClient._complete_tools recorded it as model_error and the provider or client cause is unknown.

What this means

  • The model-call boundary caught a failure without a more specific structured category, leaving the underlying provider or client cause unestablished. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • The model-call boundary caught a failure without a more specific structured category, leaving the underlying provider or client cause unestablished.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the occurrence stage and safe exception type with endpoint health; preserve reproducible failures for the client/provider owner instead of assuming a missing dependency.

How to fix it

  • Read the llm.error trace event (provider_diagnostic and error_detail) for this call and run Model routing › Check saved model (POST /api/agent/model-routing/primary/diagnostics). If a healthy endpoint keeps producing model_error, keep the trace and report it so a specific error kind can be added; inspect tool receipts before continuing the run.
  • Inspect safe provider diagnostics and endpoint health. Preserve this occurrence if a healthy endpoint repeatedly fails; inspect retained tool receipts before continuing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The same model boundary produces a complete accepted decision after the identified cause is repaired.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
